Domain is a scalar string or nonempty sequential list<string>. Scalars use domain; every list, including singleton, uses domain-1/domain-2 starting at 1. Malformed lists reject after metadata reset before I/O. Preserve order, duplicates, empty strings and exact bytes; do not lowercase, sort, deduplicate or validate domain syntax.

All six optional null arguments omit and retain server defaults; empty strings and integer zero are supplied. Allowed filename characters default to A-Z and 0-9, extension to empty, random count to 100 (documented minimum 1), relative path to .well-known/pki-validation relative to the DOMAIN DOCUMENT ROOT, max redirects to null (minimum 0), and the user-agent default can change. Zero max redirects means no limit on redirect returns; a supplied N yields N+1 redirect records so excess failures are visible. No client defaults or new integer minimum/range guards are sent.

PR109 review 5726048230 on 11.138.0.19, both routes: the handler reads one dcv_file_allowed_characters value and decodes it with Cpanel::JSON::Load, and its POD calls it a JSON-encoded arrayref. Repeated fields, even a single one, failed with a JSON parse error, so the typed method omits this option and the server default A-Z and 0-9 applies. To send it, use uapi()->call('DCV', 'check_domains_via_http', [...]) with dcv_file_allowed_characters set to caller-serialized JSON array text, for example json_encode(['a', 'b']). A typed JSON-list encoding is follow-up work.

Results preserve input order for positional domain association; no top-row domain field is pinned. Optional failure_reason is string|null, redirects is a possibly-empty list or null and redirects_count is int|null. Redirect fields remain optional: content/protocol/reason/url strings, status int and success exactly empty string|0|1; success 0 or empty string is not an envelope failure. headers is an opaque object with arbitrary values; nested redirects is list<opaque object>|null, not an inferred recursive model. Unknown fields survive only inside those opaque nodes; known objects retain existing filtering.
